newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - May 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - May 14.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Wednesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Digital Equipment Corp has filed a patent-infringement lawsuit against Intel Corp alleging Intel's Pentium microprocessors were built using patented semiconductor technology.
* International Business Machines Corp hit an all-time intraday high, signaling the computer maker's comeback.
* About 8,200 union workers went on strike at General Motors Corp's Warren, Ohio, parts-making complex.
* Retail sales dropped 0.3 percent in April.
* J.C. Penney Co Inc, Dillard Department Stores Inc, TJX Cos Inc and Lands' End Inc all issued earnings.
* Novartis AG agreed to buy the insecticide and fungicide lines of Merck and Co Inc for $910 million.
* Compaq Computer Corp plans to hire 2,000 sales people in 1997 to improve its customer contact in the wake of its failed effort to acquire Gateway 2000 Inc.
* The former brokerage firm of A.R. Baron and 13 former employees were indicted on charges of defrauding investors.
* Delta Air Lines Inc Chief Executive Ronald Allen did not shed any light on his planned departure in a meeting with analysts.
* Charles Schwab Corp plans to increase the minimum investment to $2,500 from $1,000 for other firms' funds.
* News Corp Ltd is getting closer to a $1 billion deal for International Family Entertainment Inc, but a demand by IFE controlling family's may be a sticking point.
* Procter & Gamble Co has signed a 10-year deal with Regeneron Pharmaceuticals Inc to develop and market new drugs.
* Nomura Securities Co Ltd and three executives were charged by Japanese regulators with illegally compensating a client for investment losses.
* National Education Corp agreed to an $800 million takeover by Harcourt General Inc.
* The Dow Jones industrials dropped 18.54 points to 7274.21.
* The planned merger of Grand Metropolitan Plc and Guinness Plc is forcing spirit makers to review their strategies.
* The head of Ford Motor Co's Brazil unit said new products and cost-cutting measures should cut in half the loss it posted in the prior year.

* Heard on the Street: Wall Street has made it official: Big Blue is back. International Business Machines stock yesterday blew past its all-time intraday high and came within a whisper of its closing high set a decade ago, capping the computer maker's recovery from a near-death experience in the early 1990s.
* Credit Markets: Bonds lost ground yesterday amid concerns that the economy may not be slowing fast enough to forestall a Federal Reserve interest-rate increase on Tuesday.
((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610))
